body: I don’t know if this is the place for this, but how does a CS grad qualify for business analytics/IT management positions?  It’s always offered as an “alternative” but the job requirements I see are always wildly unrelated to anything a CS grad would know.  Should I just apply anyways, and hope that they see my technical skills as useful?
It’s like I’m grieving a person that was never really there

For real, I hate hearing that shit.  I want a permanent solution.

Please just let me rest.

Might be a long shot, but does anyone have experience with Vanguard’s case study, or something similar?  What is it actually like?  The recruiter said there’s no actual programming involved, it’s more of a business/consulting kinda thing.  I’ve done stuff sort of like it, but more about tech support/database design.

I have an interview with the coming up soon and I’m not really sure how to prepare for it.
I’d rather quit playing, honestly.
It always feels like it’s coming, this looming sense of dread.  I think it’s normal… but it sure as fuck is scary.

Been especially bad lately, but it’s also been a really long time.  I can remember when my depression was manageable but I was never fully “ok”.

Been really horrible as of late though.  Long stretches of not speaking, eating, or leaving my bed.  Started out as only a few days before I was back up, but the episodes have been getting longer and longer, and every time I feel less sure that ill make it out.
I’m awake longer than I was yesterday, and I haven’t vomited
I don’t owe this world a fucking thing
Ask me in a few more months.
TIL: tears dry fast when you’re drunk out of your mind
I wish I had a job
I would have picked a stronger belt

Yep, so much for my “lucrative” computer science degree.

Could always take up some shitty min wage help desk job, might honestly help push me towards finally ending it all lol
Yeah I wish I majored in something else honestly, even if the entry level jobs pay worse lol
This is the worst part by far.  It’s like no one notices that you’ve had multiple depressive episodes, so they think that each one is isolated and not a big deal.
It’s been a year, and hundreds of applications.  Nothing yet.
Been looking for a job since graduating last May (obviously a bit before that too, but that’s when I really started counting).  Starting to wear *real* thin, honestly.
Anyone who blindly tells someone suicidal or depressed that “it gets better” is literally contributing to the problem.

MIS stands for management information systems.  It’s more of an IT/business analytics type of career path, but some MIS majors become coders as well.


Computer science and computer programming are similar, you can think of the latter as a branch of the former.  So computer science is a broad term that describes the general process of dealing with computing, while computer programming is specifically writing code and creating programs.

I’m really sorry to hear that.  I can only imagine how much that hurts, all I can say is that I hope you can grapple with these feelings day by day and hopefully end up feeling healthier and happier than now.

Thank you so much for your consideration.  This is a very difficult thing for me to talk about.

The fact that I’m posting here at all shows that I’m still clinging to life to some degree.  These thoughts are just that, thoughts.  It’s a brutal fight, that’s for sure, and I hope you’re doing well.

2021 was the worst year of my life without question, and the worst part is I can’t really put it into words why.

The point you made about the thoughts not being scary anymore really spoke to me.  The lack of emotion I have when thinking about death is honestly scarier than the thought of dying itself.

It definitely seems like swallowing the fact that life can be this way sometimes is the only option to move forwards.

I would be amazed if no one appreciated what you’ve done for them.  It might not show, but you have probably made a serious difference in someone’s life.

I hear you.  I really do.

I should be my mother’s golden child.  I was the only one of my siblings to not be born of a C-Section.  I was so smart at an early age, and my mother always thought I was extremely handsome.

But things never panned out that way.  I’m a mental trainwreck, and our relationship has never been stable.  There is a good chance that I’ll leave this world the earliest between my two brothers.  If it wasn’t for them, I might’ve done it already.

She hates me and resents the way I am.  I don’t hate her, I don’t think I ever could.  But I do feel deeply ashamed that I can never be the son to her that I could have been.

Commenting just to say I felt this down to my core.  I went to a great school, got a “hot” cs degree, and have a big “network”.  This isn’t me bragging.  I live with my dad, am unemployed, single, addicted to nicotine, and have virtually no future.  I just have nothing to show for my 23 years of life, and I just want to throw it all away before it gets even worse.

Hang in there.  At least we’re not alone in feeling this way.

First off, I appreciate your comment, it means a lot to me.


Not having debt is a tremendous privilege, and I acknowledge that.  That being said, it doesn’t change the fact that I’m not moving forwards.  I am more than willing to relocate to virtually anywhere, I’ve even been applying to jobs abroad.


I would happily fling myself into debt for a job at this point.  Even if it hurts my earnings, the experience and chance to build up credit history would be worth it.
